messages:
maria-billing: FYI ACME (acct: acme-corp) says they got billed twice for the same subscription period. Invoices INV-2026-1142 and INV-2026-1143. One was created from PO PO-9982, the other paid by card (****4242). Please investigate and do a refund/reversal as appropriate.

jordan-support: Oof. Can you confirm amounts + customer email? Also need the txn IDs if available.

maria-billing: Amounts are both $12,000.00 USD. Email: billing@acme.com. Txns: TX_1A2B3 (card), TX_4C5D6 (PO payment recorded by our AR). Customer says PO submitted first, then they saw a pending card charge and asked us to pay the card which went through.

alek-finops: TL;DR probably a race where PO workflow created an invoice and then card flow also created one. We should void one invoice and refund the card charge. Which invoice is marked paid in system?
\jmdev: DEVIN-ENG: I pulled ledger: INV-2026-1142 status=paid (card, TX_1A2B3), INV-2026-1143 status=posted (PO, applied manually by AR). Looks like AR applied the PO after card already cleared.

devin-eng: I also checked webhook logs around 2026-11-12T09:20Z — saw two invoice.created events with different ids but same subscription and no idempotency-key header on the PO flow:

```
POST /internal/webhooks/invoice.created 200
payload: {"subscription_id":"sub_95","amount":1200000,"source":"po_flow"}
POST /internal/webhooks/invoice.created 200
payload: {"subscription_id":"sub_95","amount":1200000,"source":"card_flow"}
```

Seems both flows created invoices because the PO handler doesn't attach idempotency_key. I can patch that but for now we need immediate customer remediation.

alek-finops: For remediation: 1) refund the card txn TX_1A2B3 (customer asked to keep PO), 2) mark INV-2026-1142 refunded/void, 3) confirm INV-2026-1143 stays as the canonical invoice tied to PO-9982, 4) send corrected receipts and VAT/tax adjustment if needed.

maria-billing: Agreed. Customer prefers refund to card and keep PO. I'll issue the refund once we have the provider refund id to track.

jordan-support: @payments-bot can you start the refund for TX_1A2B3 and attach refund id here? Also add note about duplicate invoice origin (webhook race) and CC legal if VAT implications.

payments-bot: Initiating refund: refund_id REF-2026-77 created for TX_1A2B3, amount=12000.00 USD. Status=processing. Reason: duplicate charge (customer request). Reference: INV-2026-1142.

legal-ops: Quick flag — if invoice INV-2026-1142 had VAT applied and was already reported, we may need a credit note. Please mark for tax review.

alek-finops: Will do. I'll open a ticket with tax team and add journal entries once refund settled. Also creating a reversal entry for revenue recognition.

devin-eng: Patch coming to add idempotency_key on PO flow and a dedupe check on invoice creation. I can push a hotfix to staging now and prod patch after signoff. Repro steps I used: 1) POST invoice.created from card_flow 2) POST invoice.created from po_flow without idempotency_key -> two invoices. I'll include the exact curl in the follow-up.

maria-billing: Payments bot now shows refund status updated.

payments-bot: Refund REF-2026-77 status=completed. Provider refund tx id RPROV_9X8Y7. Posted refund to ledger, updated INV-2026-1142 -> refunded.

jordan-support: Great. Maria — please send updated receipts to billing@acme.com, include credit note for VAT if needed, and confirm PO remains applied to INV-2026-1143.

maria-billing: Sent receipts and credit note draft to customer. Confirming INV-2026-1143 is the active invoice and linked to PO-9982. Customer acknowledged, says refund hit their bank in 3-5 business days.

alek-finops: Internal follow-ups: TAX-149 (VAT review), FIN-320 (revenue reversal journal), CODE-788 (idempotency hotfix). I will update the customer-facing ticket with links.

devin-eng: I'll schedule a short postmortem doc and include the webhook logs and patch plan.

jordan-support: Closing loop here — @maria-billing please re-open if anything else. :white_check_mark:
